claim:
Round 6 wrote VAP-r5-05's manifest row (§13.2, l. 18364–18365): "Their `manifest.json` holds one row per file, and one per derived fixture a volume names — a run-time, test-side mutation of one file, never written as a file (V12 §1b's `<dossier>@pop×k` levels; V08 §7.1's crisis, force and required-keys fixtures)".
The volumes name many more run-time mutations than the parenthesis lists, and V08 keeps two classes:
- V08 §7.1 (l. 3243–3247): "Fixtures are §13.2's frozen dossier set … plus test-side mutations of a fixture's digest or JSON made by the harness at run time, never written back into a fixture file. V12's item-122 and item-125 fixtures are test-side mutations made here (X-V12-5), each in §13.2's frozen manifest". So some mutations are registered and the rest are not.
- The tests name further mutations of their own: T-V7-69's two village mutations (written this round), T-V9-85's copy whose reconstruction condition the dossier names not (this round), T-V10-52's copy whose plague is unnamed, T-V8-36's `city-1` mutated to 8 000 people, and T-V8-61 (a)'s reductions and status mutations.
Read literally, "one per derived fixture a volume names" gives each of these a manifest row. Read with V08 §7.1 and the parenthesis, only those that V12's specs look up by id take one. V12's spec field `dossier` is "a fixture id of the frozen manifest" (V12 l. 633). One harness registers every test's mutation and another only V12's ids. Nothing in the product or in a bar's outcome changes, so the grade is minor.
required_change: §13.2's sentence: "and one per derived fixture a volume names — a run-time, test-side mutation of one file, never written as a file (V12 §1b's `<dossier>@pop×k` levels; V08 §7.1's crisis, force and required-keys fixtures):" → "and one per derived fixture a spec or bar refers to by its fixture id — a run-time, test-side mutation of one file, never written as a file (V12 §1b's `<dossier>@pop×k` levels; V08 §7.1's crisis, force and required-keys fixtures, X-V12-5); a mutation a test makes inside its own run and names only in its own text (V08 §7.1's other test-side mutations; V07's T-V7-69, V09's T-V9-85 and V10's T-V10-52 copies) takes no row:". This can be written in the same block as VCS-r6-05's field comments.

claim: VAP-r5-05's new row type (§13.2, base l. 18369–18374) adds `kind: 'derived'` and `derivedFrom?: { file; mutation }`. A derived fixture is 'never written as a file'. `DossierFixtureRow` still requires `file`, `seed` ('the synthetic seed the file was generated from'), `config`, `generatedBy`, `population` and `ourRung` on every row, and says nothing of them for a derived row. V12 §1b names a derived fixture by its id, '`<dossier>@pop×k`' (V12 l. 633: 'a fixture id of the frozen manifest'), and the row has no id field but `file`. A `@pop×k` row's population and rung are not its source's. One harness keys the row by its source's file, another by the derived id, and V12's `dossier` lookup misses in one of them. This is test-kit only.
required_change: §13.2's `DossierFixtureRow`, two comment changes. (1) `file: string` takes the comment '/* the row's fixture id (V12 §1b's `dossier`): a file's name, or for a `derived` row the id its volume names — `<file>@pop×k`, or V08 §7.1's fixture name — naming no file */'. (2) `derivedFrom`'s comment adds '; its provenance fields (`sfLine` to `generatedBy`) are its source row's, its `population`, `tierWord` and `ourRung` those of the mutated dossier'.
